Scope and authority: reviewed ONLY quality point 26. All task-relative citations below are rooted at .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task (T); rules-relative citations are rooted at .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/rules (R). Direct openpyxl inspection of R/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks!A27:D27 confirms check 26 says: "Every requirement the prompt states maps to at least one criterion (no asked-for behavior goes ungraded). Reports every gap." Read all populated Quality Checks and Deterministic Checks rows and Internal Quality Checks row 27; the latter's flow annotation does not override qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md, Specific lessons, which requires independent outcome credit and says a browser exchange cannot prove SQLite, React or TypeScript. R/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md:112-114 requires a requirement-to-criterion map. Parsed all five frozen judge.toml files: Render 1, Constraints 1, Functional 58, Polish 7, Visual 6 (73 total). Read all five prompts, injected app_context, the complete public brief, all six notes and seed.

Requirement -> criterion map (criterion IDs are the actual frozen names; protocol references locate their complete evidence instructions):
1. instruction.md:1,7 and overview.md:3 require useful editable browser code, adjacent preview/console, ready startup, examples and a fresh draft. Render/cw_workspace_runs_authored_marker (gates/render/judge.toml:23-27) proves an actual new authored JS Run. Functional/cw_startup_ready, cw_usable_examples and cw_example_separate (functional/judge.toml:25-43; prompt S01:119-121) own automatic startup, example execution/editing and saving a separate edited example without changing its original. New drafts are actually created in S21 and S22, with distinct identities and later retrieval graded by cw_saved_record_fidelity.
2. instruction.md:1 and overview.md:5; behaviour.md:27 require .js/.html/.css filename dispatch without synchronizing another selector, case-insensitively. Functional/cw_js_html_filename_dispatch, cw_css_apply_snapshot and cw_extension_case (judge:46-64; prompt S02:128-145) cover JS, complete HTML, CSS and all three uppercase extensions, with a lowercase fallback to keep dispatch separate from case correctness.
3. behaviour.md:5 requires a fresh JS document, complete HTML replacement, CSS on a fresh copy of the most recent successful document/styles, without rerunning scripts or preserving handlers/timers. Functional/cw_js_fresh_document (judge:67-71; S02:138-145 and S04:171-182), cw_js_html_filename_dispatch (S02:132-134), cw_css_apply_snapshot, cw_css_inert_copy and cw_css_pending_timer_cancelled (judge:53-85; S02:133-149) respectively cover document/global freshness, replacement, retained style/content, inert script/handler state and pending-timer cancellation. The pre-first-success built-in CSS document is a permission ("a simple built-in document is fine"), not an extra prescribed design.
4. behaviour.md:7 and security.md:3 require supersession/Stop to cancel old activity, a Stop reason, and no stale logs, errors, DOM replacements or success. Functional/cw_supersede_pending, cw_stop_pending_execution and cw_stop_pending_rollback (judge:102-120; S04:168-182) cover pending timers against an executed matching positive control. cw_completed_stop (judge:95-99; S03:160-162) separately stops an already-completed interactive preview. CSS replacement's pending timer has its own owner above.
5. behaviour.md:9 and security.md:5 require a five-second total supported-source/callback budget, a time-limit reason and usable recovery. Functional/cw_literal_loop_deadline and cw_literal_loop_rollback (judge:151-162; S09:234-247) exercise braced/unbraced literal loops and a looping Promise callback. cw_callback_shared_run_deadline and cw_callback_timeout_rollback (judge:417-428; S36:401-409) distinguish the original run budget from incorrectly refreshed nested-timer budgets. Ordinary authored function callbacks also execute in S02/S03/S04/S36. Native blocking/generated code is expressly outside the promise and is not an omitted mandatory probe.
6. behaviour.md:11 requires later click/key/input interaction after successful completion, until Stop, failure or replacement. Functional/cw_later_interactions and cw_completed_stop (judge:88-99; S03:156-162) use separate six-second idle intervals and genuine click, keyboard and input markers. No post-Stop handler survival is demanded.
7. instruction.md:3 and behaviour.md:13 require provisional failures/Stop/timeout to preserve or restore the latest successful render, not a half-failed candidate or an older success. Functional/cw_stop_pending_rollback, cw_literal_loop_rollback, cw_js_error_rollback, cw_html_error_rollback, cw_timer_error_rollback, cw_promise_error_rollback and cw_callback_timeout_rollback own their stated outcomes; S10:253-260 explicitly establishes successful A then B and checks rollback to B. S03/S04/S09-S13/S36 permit static restored pictures and optional pending candidate display, consistent with the public requirement.
8. behaviour.md:15 requires source error message and one-based entered-source lines, counting all HTML pre-script lines, also for timer errors and unhandled Promise rejections. Functional/cw_js_error_message, cw_js_error_line, cw_html_error_message, cw_html_error_line, cw_timer_error_message, cw_timer_error_line, cw_promise_error_message and cw_promise_error_line (judge:165-246; S10-S13:253-300) own the four specified error paths. Coverage is incomplete for the explicitly promised HTML asynchronous coordinate cases: see G3.
9. behaviour.md:19 requires ordered log/warn/error/info levels, expandable objects/arrays, retained recent history, Clear and the duration of each run. Functional/cw_console_level_stream, cw_console_value_inspection, cw_console_history, cw_console_clear_control and cw_console_duration (judge:249-281; S14-S16:306-328) cover these features. S15 actually opens nested object values and array elements; retained-history bounds are permitted. Duration coverage stops at one successful completion: see G4.
10. behaviour.md:21 requires pause-based automatic execution with debounce restart on later edits, idle off-state, cancellation of a queued run when switched off, and manual Run in both states. Functional/cw_autorun_debounce, cw_autorun_off_stays_idle, cw_autorun_off_cancels_queue and cw_manual_run_independent_of_autorun (judge:284-309; S17:334-340) cover each outcome with actual automatic positive controls, a measured observation window and an on-state manual Run without an edit debounce.
11. overview.md:7, behaviour.md:25, integration.md:7 and policy.md:3 require a shared local library with identities/title/filename/exact source, New as a distinct record, updates to the loaded identity and exact load/reload fidelity. Constraints/cw_saved_source_shared_across_clean_contexts (constraints/judge.toml:23-29) observes a successful UI save and server-supplied retrieval in a clean independent context. Functional/cw_saved_record_fidelity and cw_saved_records_browser_reload (judge:333-344; S21:354-357 and S23:376-379) cover new identities, exact fields, reload and in-place update. cw_example_separate covers separation from bundled examples.
12. integration.md:7 requires process-restart persistence of identities, revisions and fields, no duplicate seeding. Functional/cw_process_restart_durability (judge:347-351; S22:363-365) records all identities/titles and exact fields/revisions for two independent records before the single actual restart, then checks once-only retrieval. cw_process_restart_write (judge:354-358; S22:366-369) separately owns writing afterward, including an independent fresh-record fallback.
13. behaviour.md:27 requires trimming and case-sensitive uniqueness of every saved title, rejecting empty/whitespace or colliding titles with feedback and unchanged records. Functional/cw_title_trimming, cw_title_collision_refusal, cw_title_empty_rejected and cw_title_case_sensitive (judge:375-400; S24:386-389) test create/update trimming, valid case-distinct creation and invalid CURRENT-REVISION UPDATES. The invalid new-record create branches have no witness: see G2.
14. behaviour.md:29 and instruction.md:3 require a revision on every accepted saved change, stale Save refusal without changed fields/revision, all dirty fields retained, useful recovery and repetition with editor roles reversed. Functional/cw_stale_save_server_refusal and cw_stale_save_draft_recovery (judge:361-372; S23:375-380) own independent server-refusal and real-editor retention/recovery evidence in both cycles. S21 owns update identity fidelity; S22/S23 observe advanced revisions. Proactive explained prevention with exact draft retention is valid; server request replay alone cannot establish editor recovery.
15. security.md:3 requires preview isolation from parent document/origin storage and protection of current app state. Functional/cw_preview_origin_boundary (judge:123-127; S05:188-198) performs all four document/storage read/write attempts, verifies actual unchanged parent state and brackets them with successful own-document execution. The current-preview lifecycle restriction also maps to cancellation/completed-Stop/CSS outcomes above.
16. security.md:7 and policy.md:5 require clearly refusing eval, Function, WebAssembly, workers and dynamic import, with good preview/recovery, while words in comments/strings/HTML text remain valid. Functional/cw_harmless_scope_words and cw_unsupported_execution_refused (judge:137-148; S08:214-228) cover the harmless control and FIVE separate bounded family probes, with an independent last-good fallback. No unrequested alias/bypass catalogue is inferred.
17. security.md:9 permits external app assets but forbids authored-snippet external resources/services. Functional/cw_snippet_network_boundary (judge:130-134; S07:204-208 plus supplied routing recipe:27-95) uses matching working transport controls and separate fetch/Image attempts, counts delivery and checks visible refusal/recovery. All prompts permit app CDN assets and the alternate local loopback preview hostname. The stated representative network boundary is covered; lack of an unbounded exploit catalogue is not itself a point-26 defect.
18. security.md:11 says save/load store source as text and "Source entered into the editor is never evaluated on the server." Exact text roundtrip maps to Constraints and cw_saved_record_fidelity, but the no-server-execution promise has no owner or distinguishing observation: see G1.
19. instruction.md:7 and ui.md:3,5,7,9 require three useful panes, narrow-screen access, editor monospace/line numbers/syntax colouring, requested controls, light/dark workspace themes, labelled controls, visible keyboard focus, pointer-free navigation and legibility. Functional/cw_editor_monospace, cw_editor_line_numbers, cw_editor_syntax_colouring (judge:312-330; S19:346-348) cover editor mechanics. cw_theme_actual_switch and cw_theme_work_preserved (judge:403-414; S34:395) exercise both theme transitions while preserving state; authored preview recolouring is optional. Polish/responsive_layout (polish/judge:23), cw_controls_have_names, cw_controls_keyboard_reachable, cw_controls_focus_visible and cw_keyboard_library_navigation (polish/judge:32,41,50,59; prompt P02:43-49) cover 390x844 use, all requested enabled controls, actual focus and a pointer-free editor->example->saved-item->editor route. interaction_feedback and workspace_organisation (polish/judge:68,77) cover clear acknowledgement and locatable surfaces. Visual/visual_typography, visual_color_and_contrast, visual_spacing_and_layout, visual_hierarchy_and_scanability, visual_overall_craft and visual_responsive_consistency (visual/judge:24-104; visual/prompt:17-22,35-37) cover desktop craft, both offered themes and cross-viewport composition while Polish owns mobile operability. No exact colour, layout, control label, shortcut hint or editor package is required.
20. instruction.md:1, overview.md:7 and policy.md:3 require no accounts/sign-in. Render opens without sign-in; both gates and all scored in-dimension prerequisites use the public shared library. No authentication criterion is imposed. policy.md:5 freedoms over labels, indentation, routes and request fields are respected by UI-purpose matching and discovery of actual request formats. instruction.md:9 / security.md:9 / policy.md:7 permit app external assets; no same-origin demand is added.
21. Runtime/deliverable requirements in instruction.md:5,9 and integration.md:3-11 are only partly assured by the grading profile. test.sh:68 checks server.js presence, :97-111 starts Node on PORT 3000 with DB_PATH and NODE_PATH, and :48 probes health/root; Constraints checks health and the local server-backed save/read. S22 grades restart behavior. The frozen template itself mandates Node/Express/better-sqlite3, SQLite/DB_PATH, one process and no external backend (R/projects/webdev-task-template/environment/instructions/integration.md). Exact Express/SQLite use, single process count, absence of a proxy to an external backend, honouring a non-default DB_PATH under the normal writable-/app path, and 0.0.0.0 rather than loopback binding are not established by matching browser data. Task-specific source/build-file delivery, /app/public/index.html placement, absence of startup installation and independence from runtime /assets or /instructions likewise have no independent browser criterion. Some are exercised indirectly by successful startup in the separate image, but startup is not proof of all these literal assurances. This is a declared runtime/profile assurance limit, not evidence of a bad reference implementation or a new requirement to inspect source. React/TypeScript/Vite are expressly optional (integration.md:3), so there is NO missing mandatory frontend-stack check. Keep canonical harness/settings unchanged; resolve exact-stack assurance centrally rather than silently adding browser-source inspection or calling the constraint gate proof of SQLite.

Credible product coverage defects:
G1 (P1, task-specific security promise, source-confirmed / counterexample runtime NOT EXERCISED): security.md:11 promises server non-evaluation. No criterion covers it. Constraints:25-29 and S21/S22/S23/S24 only compare stored text and records; Functional prompt:7 forbids implementation/database inspection and limits evidence to product actions. A plausible otherwise-correct implementation evaluates each saved/loaded .js string in a bounded server VM for validation/metadata, suppresses VM console/errors and then stores/returns the original bytes. It produces every prescribed preview/library outcome while directly violating this promise. Browser roundtrip is not evidence of non-evaluation. Add a bounded save/load execution-boundary outcome with a supported observable negative witness and explicit limits, or resolve the absolute implementation assurance through approved profile policy; do not simply award it from storage fidelity.
G2 (P1, ungraded invalid creation branch, source-confirmed / mutant runtime NOT EXERCISED): behaviour.md:25 distinguishes new drafts from updates and :27 applies nonempty/unique titles to saved snippets generally. Yet S24:387-388 probes ONLY Source's CURRENT revision and observed Save-update format; all new records in S01/S21/S22/S23/S24, Constraints and Polish have valid unique titles. A product that trims on create but omits empty/duplicate checks in its create UI/endpoint, while correctly validating all updates, meets every written scenario. Its users can create empty or duplicate records. Extend the existing title outcomes with ordinary New/Save invalid-create probes and corresponding valid-create controls, checking the complete library unchanged, without assuming POST/PUT routes or schemas.
G3 (P2, missing HTML asynchronous error-coordinate branches, source-confirmed / mutant runtime NOT EXERCISED): behaviour.md:15 explicitly says HTML line numbers count from the complete document, followed by "The same applies to errors thrown later by a timer and to unhandled Promise rejections." S11:267-277 uses only synchronous undefinedFunctionCall at document line 6. S12:285-288 uses delayed-error.js line 2; S13:296-299 uses rejected-promise.js line 2. A compiler that applies HTML's pre-script offset only in its synchronous catch, leaving timer/rejection handlers to report inline-script-relative lines, passes all four scenarios but misreports the required asynchronous HTML lines. Add bounded complete-HTML timer and rejection fixtures with markup before their script, reusing existing error/line/rollback owners and setup observations.
G4 (P2, missing duration observations for non-success outcomes, source-confirmed / mutant runtime NOT EXERCISED): behaviour.md:19 says "Show how long each run took." cw_console_duration at functional/judge.toml:274 narrows this to "The completed Run shows a measured duration" and S16:326 observes only console.log('history-first') success. S03/S04/S09-S13/S36 require reasons, errors, rollback/recovery, but never require an elapsed duration for their stopped, failed or timed-out run. Polish:68 accepts status, new output OR an empty state, so it cannot fill this gap. An implementation displaying elapsed time only on successful completion, hiding it on error/Stop/timeout, passes those prescribed observations. Reuse the already-performed lifecycle scenarios to record their displayed elapsed durations under the duration owner; do not repeat expensive scenarios.

Conforming-alternative challenge: traced a vanilla-JS frontend (the named React/TypeScript/Vite tools are optional), a server-rendered library without a separate JSON list route, arbitrary API labels/fields, proactive stale-Save prevention, a static rollback snapshot, a pending overlay and ordinary undocumented editor Escape/Tab behavior through the written checks. Render:27, Constraints:27-29, Functional prompt:11-21, app_context:12,18 and Polish prompt:29-30 explicitly admit these choices; none supplies grounds for a false fail. This is a source-level fairness check, not a claim that such an alternate app was launched. In particular, an app using another durable engine could be observationally equivalent, but that would violate the inherited stack requirement; it is an assurance limitation, not a conforming alternative.

Raw evidence checked (not another review): qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json and its executed drivers. Recomputed SHA256 values match RESULTS.functional_sha256 (8e309112e55b495ff94bcc420483dc844b865bdf93cd3008522829914c2f3a2d) and prompt_sha256 (6405c6c52916b9480837a98b228a26e5fa0465241a3003d6da71b5f2bab907d1). Driver hashes for current_flow.cjs, runtime_flow.cjs and run_workflow.cjs also match the raw manifest. run_workflow.cjs:34 selects current_flow for S24, so unused legacy S24 code was not mistaken for the executed probe. current_flow.cjs:25-40 creates valid unique sources, then sends all four invalid titles through update.operation; RESULTS facts S24.title_collision_refusal and S24.title_empty_rejected record refusals and unchanged records under that update-only scope. RESULTS S11.html_error_line records bad.html line 6; S12.timer_error_line records delayed-error.js line 2; S13.promise_error_line records rejected-promise.js line 2. RESULTS S16.console_duration records "Complete ? 3.8 ms". Other raw observations incidentally contain durations (e.g. S04 "Run cancelled ? 58.5 ms" and S09 timeout statuses), showing the golden offers them; no current duration criterion demands those observations. Golden success cannot refute a missing rubric branch. None of G1-G4's wrong-app witnesses was executed in this audit. No paid/configured judge, Oracle score, target-model result or judge completion-time inference is made.
counterexample: Four plausible source-audited false-pass witnesses, not executed: (1) save/load run the text in a bounded server VM with no visible outputs before returning the original bytes; (2) New/Save creates blank or duplicate titles while update validation is complete; (3) only synchronous HTML errors receive the document-line offset, leaving HTML timer/rejection lines script-relative; (4) elapsed duration appears only for successful runs. Each preserves the observations currently demanded by all five dimensions. The detailed requirement and protocol citations are in evidence.
suggested_fix: Add bounded save/load execution-boundary evidence or resolve that absolute assurance through approved profile policy; add invalid new-title creation cases; add asynchronous complete-HTML line fixtures; collect duration from existing error/Stop/timeout scenarios. Preserve independent outcome ownership and reuse existing setups. Keep inherited exact-stack/runtime assurance limits explicit and do not alter the canonical harness, budgets, policy, or browser-source ban.
